label: Attestations and assurance reports
summary: An independent party reports on the organisation's controls: a CPA firm for SOC 2 and SOX, an external assessor for HITRUST, a CSA-accredited body for STAR. Management writes a system description and signs an assertion; the window in which controls must operate is fixed before it opens.

requires_org.reason: The system description and the assessed platforms are drawn from the key systems.
Subservice and service organisations must be listed with their report method.
Management signs the assertion or representation letter.

source.ref: AICPA SOC 2 pages and audit-firm guides (categories, Type 1 and 2, observation window); SEC and PCAOB rules for ICFR; CSA STAR levels; HITRUST Assessment Handbook (e1, i1, r2)

fields.label: Report type
fields.note: Type I reports design as of a date; Type II reports operation over a period. Customers usually want Type II; many start with Type I.

fields.label: Report date
fields.note: The single date the design of the controls is reported as of.

fields.label: Categories
fields.note: Security is always in; add the others only where customers need them. The auditor asks why each was chosen.

fields.label: Why these
fields.note: The customer need behind each category, from contracts and questionnaires.

fields.label: Window start
fields.note: First day of the observation period. Controls must operate from here; a window opened before controls work is the commonest failure.

fields.label: Window end
fields.note: Last day of the period. AICPA sets no minimum; six to twelve months is usual, three can be accepted for a new service with the reason disclosed.

fields.label: CPA firm
fields.note: The independent service auditor (SOC 2) or external auditor (SOX). Readiness work by the same firm is limited by independence rules.

fields.label: Assertion signatory
fields.note: The executive who signs management's assertion, dated the same as the auditor's report.

fields.label: Filer status

source.ref: Sarbanes-Oxley s.302 and s.404 and the SEC filer-status definitions; auditor attestation (404(b)) depends on filer status

fields.note: Applies directly to SEC registrants. A subsidiary is in scope through its parent's group assessment; a service provider supports its customers' assessments.

fields.label: Fiscal year end
fields.note: Management assesses ICFR as of year end; testing is planned backwards from it.

fields.label: ICFR framework
fields.note: SEC guidance names COSO as a suitable framework; 2013 is the current edition.

fields.label: Prior deficiencies
fields.note: Significant deficiencies or material weaknesses reported last year, and whether they are closed. The auditor starts from them.

fields.label: Assessment type

source.ref: HITRUST Assessment Handbook v1.2: validated types e1, i1, r2; readiness assessments carry no HITRUST quality review

fields.note: e1 and i1 are valid for 1 year, r2 for 2 years with an interim assessment before the first anniversary. Readiness only cannot be certified.

fields.label: Scope factors
fields.note: The organisational, geographic, system and regulatory factors that tailor an r2 assessment. HITRUST derives the control set from them.

fields.label: Interim due
fields.note: The r2 interim assessment falls in the last 90 days before the first anniversary of the certificate.

fields.label: External assessor
fields.note: A separate firm approved by HITRUST. Its staff must not have implemented the controls in the last 12 months.

fields.label: Letter signatory
fields.note: Signs the management representation letter.

fields.label: STAR level

source.ref: Cloud Security Alliance STAR programme levels

fields.note: Level 1 is a prerequisite for Level 2. Level 2 extends an existing SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit with the CCM.

fields.label: CCM version
fields.note: CSA accepts both versions until the end of 2027.

fields.label: Base audit scope
fields.note: Confirms the SOC 2 or ISO 27001 scope already covers the cloud offering being certified.

source.ref: SOC 2 description criteria (DC 200): services, commitments and requirements, components, boundaries; SOX: significant accounts to in-scope applications; HITRUST scope webforms; CSA: the cloud service offering, not the company

fields.label: Services
fields.note: The services or the specific cloud offering covered. Scoping the whole company instead of the offering is a common CSA mistake.

fields.label: Systems
fields.note: Infrastructure, software and data inside the boundary, picked from the organisation profile. For SOX include the databases, operating systems and tools that enable financial applications.

fields.label: Sites
fields.note: Locations and facilities. HITRUST requires every facility hosting an in-scope component; home offices cannot be in scope.

fields.label: Commitments
fields.note: Principal service commitments and system requirements, from contracts, SLAs and privacy notices. The auditor tests controls against them.

fields.label: Significant accounts
fields.note: Financial statement accounts and disclosures, with the applications that support each. IT scope is derived from them, top-down; only IT controls that other key controls rely on are in scope.

fields.label: Platforms
fields.note: Platforms or systems to certify: business function, hosting and whether they include an AI model. Only systems in production for at least 90 days can be certified.

fields.label: Boundary note
fields.note: What is inside the boundary and what is not, in words. Vague boundaries are the main reason descriptions are sent back.

fields.label: Responsibility owner
fields.note: Owns the shared-responsibility split (CSP, customer, third party) recorded per control.

source.ref: SOC 2 subservice organisations (carve-out or inclusive) and complementary controls; SOX reliance on SOC 1 reports; HITRUST carve-out rules

fields.label: Providers
fields.note: Hosting, SaaS and outsourced providers whose controls the system relies on, with how each is treated and which report is held. A carve-out still needs the provider's own report.

fields.label: No providers
fields.note: Tick when no provider's controls are relied on.

fields.label: User controls drafted
fields.note: Complementary user-entity controls (what the customer must run) are listed and will appear in the description.

source.ref: Audit-firm readiness guidance: control owners, evidence locations and a dry run before the window or fieldwork

fields.label: Control owners
fields.note: Every control has a named owner, an evidence location and a frequency.

fields.label: Dry run
fields.note: A readiness pass before the window opens. Failing controls should be fixed or dated before the observation starts.

fields.label: Policies approved
fields.note: Policies and procedures the controls rely on are approved.

fields.label: Kickoff date
fields.note: Engagement kickoff with the auditor or assessor.

fields.label: Report due
fields.note: When the report or opinion is needed, for example by a customer or the filing date.

gate.label: Security is among the SOC 2 categories
gate.hint: Security is mandatory in every SOC 2 report.

gate.label: Observation window ends after it starts
gate.hint: Set the first and last day of the period.

gate.label: Observation window is at least 3 months
gate.hint: Six to twelve months is what customers usually accept; annual controls need something to sample.

source.ref: Audit-firm guidance; AICPA sets no minimum

gate.label: Each carved-out provider has its report
gate.hint: A carve-out without the provider's own report cannot be relied on.

gate.label: A dry run is done
gate.hint: Run a readiness pass before the window or fieldwork opens.
